body:
An orchestrator that re-reads where things stand now sees the web environment record change, instead of "nothing new". The same goes for work waiting to land, parts that could not report, and git's copy of the board falling behind.

### What was wrong
M5's delta resume compares a snapshot of posts, comments, open questions and running sessions. The Web environment section (CL39) is computed from the project config, not from any post, so recording an environment id changed nothing in the snapshot and the second resume printed "nothing new", hiding it. Every Claude Code session has a session id, so CL39's own test was red for anyone running the suite from one.

### The change
- The orchestrator's snapshot now also holds four sections as the whole resume prints them: web environment, work not on the trunk yet, parts that could not reach their orchestrator, and git's copy behind. When one changes, the delta prints it whole under its heading (or says it cleared).
- A snapshot from before this change has no sections: nothing is compared, so no spurious change on the first run after an update.
- Checked and left out: trains past size or age (they move with the clock, every delta would show them), what the owner can do and the autonomy text (config, no action), kit commands skipped and the memory line (reports), split, start and inherit lines (made from posts and comments: already covered).

### The test
CL39's resume test now runs twice: with no session id (the whole resume each time) and with one (the second read is the delta, which must carry the environment id and the Web environment heading, never "nothing new"). On the code before this step the with-id run fails, the without-id run passes.

### The full suite with a session id
Run with this session's own id set: 79 suites passed, 0 failed. Nothing else turned red.
